sentences.text:
Author: K. Lakshman
Bench: K.Lakshman
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Lakshman
 Writ Petition No.11186 of 2023
Order:

Heard Smt Saritha Modukuru, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Gadi Praveen Kumar, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri G.Venkateswarlu, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
Perused the record.
2. The petitioner herein is holder of Passport bearing No. L4087280 and it was valid up to 05.08.2023.
He had submitted an application for renewal of the said passport, vide application No.HY75C5025459523, dated 21.03.2023 by paying requisite fee.
The respondents herein are not renewing his passport on the ground of pendency of the criminal case.
3. When the petitioner checked his passport status in online it revealed that Police Verification Report is not clear and application is under review at Regional Passport Office.

Immediately, the petitioner proceeded to Passport Office on 16.03.2023 and enquired about issuance of his passport,
for which the authorities concerned orally stated that as the petitioner involved in Cr.No.405 of 2020 of Neredmet Police Station vide C.C.No.1525 of 2022 on the file of I Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Malkajgiri, Rachakonda, Medchal District, the petitioner was rejected for renewal of his passport.
Therefore, the present Writ Petition.
4. The petitioner contends that he was falsely implicated in the aforesaid crime.
Further, he is also ready to co-operate with the trial.
Therefore, he sought to issue necessary directions to the respondents for consideration of his application to re-issue his passport.
5. Respondent No.2 cannot deny renewal of Passport on the ground that aforesaid Criminal Case is pending against him.

It is also relevant to note that the Apex Court in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu v. Central Bureau of Investigation1 had an occasion to examine the provisions of the Passports Act, pendency of criminal cases and held that refusal of a passport can be only in case where an applicant is convicted during the period of five (05) years immediately preceding the date of application for an offence involving moral turpitude and sentence for imprisonment for not less than two years.

entities.text: Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu v. Central Bureau of Investigation1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 6.2 (f) relates to a situation where the applicant is facing trial in a criminal Court.

The petitioner therein was convicted in a case for the offences under Sections - 420, 468, 471 and 477A read with 120B of the IPC and also Section - 13 (2) read with Section . 2020 Crl.L.J. (SC)
572 13 (1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Against which, an appeal was filed and the same was dismissed.
The sentence was reduced to a period of one (01) year.

The petitioner therein Ramineni Sritish vs Union Of India on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132972029/
1 had approached the Apex Court by way of filing an appeal and the same is pending.

sentences.text:
Therefore,
considering the said facts, the Apex Court held that Passport Authority cannot refuse renewal of the passport on the ground of pendency of the criminal appeal.
Thus, the Apex Court directed the Passport Authority to renew the passport of the applicant without raising the objection relating to the pendency of the aforesaid criminal case.
6. As discussed above, the aforesaid criminal case is pending against the petitioner herein.
The passport of the petitioner is valid up to 05.08.2023.
He had submitted an application on 21.03.2023 for renewal of his passport.
Respondent No.2 is not considering the application for renewal on the ground of pendency of the aforesaid criminal case.
On the ground of pendency of the proceedings in criminal cases, respondent No.2 cannot deny renewal of passport of the petitioner herein.
There is no provision in the Passports Act or Rules/ Regulations that passport cannot be granted on the ground of pendency of criminal cases.
Further, the petitioner herein is standing on better footing than the petitioner in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu1.
However, if the petitioner is intending to travel abroad, he has to approach trial Court in the aforesaid criminal case and obtain permission for travelling abroad.
In the present writ petition, the petitioner is not seeking permission to travel abroad, and he is seeking only renewal of his passport.

7. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondent No.2 herein to consider the application No.HY75C5025459523, dated 21.03.2023 submitted by the petitioner seeking renewal of his passport on the following conditions:-
i) The petitioner herein shall submit an undertaking along with an affidavit in C.C.No.1525 of 2022 on the file of I Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Malkajgiri,
Rachakonda, Medchal District, stating that he shall not leave India during pendency of the said C.C. without permission of the Court and that he shall co-operate with trial Court in concluding the proceedings in the said C.C.

sentences.text: However, liberty is granted to the petitioner herein to file an application before the learned Magistrate seeking permission to travel abroad, and it is for the learned Magistrate to consider the same in accordance with law.
However, in the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Writ Petition shall stand closed.
K. LAKSHMAN, J April 21, 2023 pss/prat

7. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondent No.2 herein to consider the application No.HY75C5025459523, dated 21.03.2023 submitted by the petitioner seeking renewal of his passport on the following conditions:-
i) The petitioner herein shall submit an undertaking along with an affidavit in C.C.No.1525 of 2022 on the file of I Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Malkajgiri,
Rachakonda, Medchal District, stating that he shall not leave India during pendency of the said C.C. without permission of the Court and that he shall co-operate with trial Court in concluding the proceedings in the said C.C.
ii) On filing such an undertaking as well as affidavit, the trial Court shall issue a certified copy of the same within two (02) weeks therefrom;
iii) The petitioner herein shall submit certified copy of this order as well as the aforesaid undertaking before the Passport Officer/ Authority concerned for renewal of his passport;
iv) On submission of the aforesaid documents, the Passport Officer/Authority shall consider the same afresh in the light of the observations made by this Court herein as well as the contents of the undertaking given by the petitioner for renewal of his passport in accordance with law, within three (03) weeks from the date of said application;
v) On renewal of the Passport, the petitioner herein shall deposit the original renewed passport before the trial Court in C.C.No.1525 of 2022 and Ramineni Sritish vs Union Of India on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132972029/
2 vi)
However, liberty is granted to the petitioner herein to file an application before the learned Magistrate seeking permission to travel abroad, and it is for the learned Magistrate to consider the same in accordance with law.
However, in the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
